walkthroughs.body_html:
Global Systems & Global Governance — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Global Systems & Global Governance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Global Systems & Global Governance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Does globalisation benefit all places equally?
options: Globalisation only affects countries on the equator.
No — flows of trade and investment concentrate in some regions while others are switched off; globalisation creates winners and losers between and within countries.
Growth in global trade automatically lifts every country in the same way.
Global governance is run by the world's largest TNC.

mcqs.q: Is global governance the same as world government?
options: The United Nations can force any country to obey its decisions.
Globalisation only affects countries on the equator.
No — global governance is the web of institutions, laws and norms, such as the UN and WTO, through which states cooperate; no single authority rules over states.
Global governance is run by the world's largest TNC.

mcqs.q: Do TNCs keep every stage of production in their home country?
options: TNCs are banned from operating in more than three countries.
Global governance is run by the world's largest TNC.
A company's products are all made in the country where the brand is based.
No — TNCs typically spread production through global supply chains, locating each stage where costs, skills and market access are best, while headquarters and research often stay at home.
